name: eos-template
description: Engineering Operating System template — a local-first, zero-dependency governance engine for VS Code + GitHub Copilot.

comments.zeroDependency: EOS has NO dependencies and no devDependencies, and that is a design constraint rather than a current fact. The whole claim is that a developer can run the entire governance loop offline with nothing but Node — `.github/eos/offline-boundary.test.mjs` asserts that EOS Core cannot even reach the network. A dependency would add a lockfile, an install step and a supply-chain surface to a tool whose job is to police exactly those things. Admitting one is an architecture decision: record an ADR in docs/adr/ first. See .github/eos/lib/schema.mjs for the same reasoning applied to a JSON-Schema validator.
comments.engines: 20.10.0 is the floor the engine actually needs (node:test reporters, os.availableParallelism). CI pins 20; development happens on 22. This range is what makes that difference deliberate rather than accidental — the skew used to be untested in both directions.
comments.scripts: Every script is a thin delegation to a .mjs entry point that also works when invoked directly. npm is a convenience for contributors, never a requirement: `node .github/eos/eos.mjs next` must keep working in a repository that has no npm at all.

scripts.verify: npm run lint && npm run doctor && npm run secrets && npm test && node .github/eos/eos.mjs ledger --verify
